recipes.name: Pork Loin Stuffed with Spinach
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Saute spinach, butter, onions and garlic over medium heat until soft. Add bread crumbs. Cut tenderloin in half lengthwise. Stuff with spinach mixture and secure with kitchen twine.

In a bowl, mix ketchup, orange juice and teriyaki sauce. Baste tenderloin with 1/2 of the mixture. Sprinkle pork with cumin. Place in shallow roaster and bake at 350 degrees uncovered for one hour. Baste with reserved marinade and cook one more hour covered. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Loin Stuffed with Spinach
raw_recipe.description: Pork loin stuffed with spinach, onion, garlic and bread crumbs, basted in a fabulous sweet sauce.

review.reviewBody:
This was a very good recipe, however I kicked it up a notch and added prosiutto and mozzarella to it.
when I spli the roast I added the prosiutto and then mozzarella, then the spinach, then another layer of mozzarella followed by another layer of prosiutto.

my wife and friens said it should have been one of the specials on the menu at a resturaunt. it came out sensational.

try it.

Yummm!!! Yes, I did make a couple of changes, after I made it the first time, which was delicious as it was written. The second time I also added prosciutto and Swiss cheese slices, then wrapped the whole thing with thick bacon slices. After I sliced the pork loin roast nearly in half, I layered 3 slices of prosciutto, then two slices of Swiss cheese, on both halves. Next I held the two sides, while I stuffed the fresh spinach mixture in, then I used Baker's twine to hold it all together. The next step was to wrap the whole roast with thick slices of smoked bacon. I placed the roast uncovered, in 400* oven for 60 minutes, then I lowered the temp to 350* for about 30 minutes, more or less, depending on the size of your roast, until the internal temp is 145*. I peeled off the bacon for the last 15 or so minutes and left it laying in the pan. It helped to make some great chunky and flavorful sauce. I will use this recipe on the beef roast next!

I made this. It’s amazing! However, I tweaked it a little. I used a hot pepper Jam on the pork before stuffing. For the stuffing I sautéed onion, garlic and fresh chopped spinach. I made stove top stuffing. I mixed spinach with the stuffing then added some cheddar cheese. I spread the stuffing mixture on the loin then rolled it up. Before putting it in the oven I sprinkled some panko crumbs across the top. Baked @. 375 for about an hour( internal temperature 150). This was outstanding!!!!!!!

I made a few tweaks. I used the whole package of spinach ( you can never have too much spinach). I used 2 cloves of garlic. I used fresh squeezed Orange juice. Instead of ketchup I used a sugar free mesquite bbq sauce. I also added mozzarella cheese in with the spinach. I only needed to cook it for about 1 1/2 hours. It was moist and delicious.

This was fantastic! I made the following adjustments -- doubled the garlic, added a sauteed red pepper, substituted crushed crackers (Kirkland signature ancient grains) for the bread crumbs for more flavour and added a cup of shredded asiago cheese. IMO the addition of cheese really makes this recipe. Finally - and this is VERY important - if you're using pork tenderloin (as opposed to pork loin) it only needs to cook 40 mins. I marinated after the first 20 mins and cooked it uncovered. Highly recommend this recipe!

I butterflied the tenderloin and pounded it out with a mallet to thin it out for quicker cooking. I then salted and peppered the inside before glazing it with the sauce and then layered some mozzarella and prosciutto followed by the spinach filling and simply folded it over. I salted and peppered the outside along with rubbing some olive oil into the meat and added some white wine and worcestershire sauce to the glaze and basted it several times during roasting. I baked it for a total of 50 minutes and left it to rest on counter for nearly 15 minutes before serving. It was so juicy and flavorful. I served it with steamed broccoli and garlic roasted fingerling potatoes. What an awesome dish. The one thing I didn't care for was the cumin. I will definitely make this again but the additional spice isnt really needed if you salt and pepper well and use plenty of glaze.

Yum, yum, yum. That's all I can say about this recipe. The only tweaking I did was use 3 garlic buds, doubled the sauce recipe (didn't have ketchup, so used Heinz chili sauce), added feta to the stuffing, and used Panko bread crumbs. Also had some of the bread/onion/garlic left over in the frying pan, so topped the tenderloin with it before putting in the oven. Definitely do not cook for suggested time - I cooked for just over an hour (read 145 on thermometer), and tented while I made the side dish. Hubby thought it was one of the best meals I have ever made, which says a lot, since he loves my cooking.

I (and the hubs) loved my version thanks to the base recipe and others' recommendations. I used fresh spinach, extra garlic (4 cloves) and I substituted stovetop stuffing for the bread crumbs, but used all the butter suggested. I ditched the ketchup-teriyaki sauce, and instead, sprinkled pepper, salt, savory, garlic powder, cumin, and olive oil on top. That add a nice crunch texture to the top layer. I cooked for about an hour at 350 and double checked with the thermometer to make sure it was all set.

I love this recipe and have made it many times. Instead of just cutting the tenderloin in half to split it, I carefully cut the roll open by cutting on an angle and rolling the meat as I go so it ends up like an open jelly roll (does that make sense?). I add feta cheese to the spinach mixture and after adding the stuffing I roll it up like a jelly roll and tie with butcher's string. Such a beautiful presentation!

I made this awesome dish & cut my pork loin so I was able to roll it jelly roll style. I added the prosciuto & mozzarella as suggested & then the stuffing. I basted it with worcestershire sauce, teriyaki sauce & dry white wine. I seasoned with salt, pepper, & rosemary. I baked as recommended, but took out at 145 degrees. I tented it while preparing side dishes. It was out of this world & the presentation was wonderful too. Thank you for this wonderful recipe.

We agreed the basic recipe was very good. But I would never have cooked it that long. I took it out at 140 degrees and tented it for 15 mins. For my family we added more garlic and some cilantro in the stuffing and more cumin in the sauce. I also make the sauce several hours ahead so the flavors meld, chill it and then bring back to room temp. And since I first made this I've learned to double the spinach stuffing mixture. It is so much better and makes the presentation even more distinct. I also have been known to add a shot or two of bourbon to the sauce!!! This is an update - I originally reviewed it years ago and continue to love it and make it often.
Family and I really liked!! I doubled the sauce.

This was an easy recipe. I used olive oil instead of the marinade, only because I don’t care for the sweet taste. To prevent it from becoming too dry, I cooked it with the fatty side up and put about a half inch of water in the bottom. Also, I rented it for the first hour, rather than the second. It came out perfectly.

this was the best pork tenderloin I have ever had. since there are only 2 of us I used 1and a half pound loin. I used all of the rest of the ingredients as if it was a 3 lb loin. I also substituted fresh spinach instead of frozen. it is now in my favorites category.
The filling is very bland. The glaze is nice, but doesn't really work with the filling at all.
Delicious! Added feta cheese to the stuffing. Only needs about 45mins - 1 hour cook time.

I've made this several times. In the beginning I made this just as written but I've changed the recipe a few times since then. I usually leave out the breadcrumbs, because I'm gluten intolerant. I've added gruyere cheese and mushrooms and sometimes leave out the spinach. My family loves it either way. I always use a pork loin, not pork tenderloin. Easily feeds 4 people.
Stuffed it with cottage cheese bake. It was a warm savory flavor. Very unique. Pork was sliced when I opened it so it looks a bit messy. very happy with it.

Delicious recipe. I did it the way they suggested as I always do with first time recipes. Next time, I will cook the pork tender line a little bit less time. I may even add a little cream cheese to the spinach, but it’s not necessary. It would just be a bit creamier. Thank you for the recipe.
Liked the glaze. Stuffing was just a lot of effort.
